identity.title: A targeting delivery platform for the mapping of responses to p53-independent intervention in heterogeneous patient cancer cells.

content.abstract: Developing new cancer therapeutic strategies has become a central focus in precision oncology. However, a major challenge is the lack of robust models to accurately assess target vulnerability in patient-specific heterogeneous cancer cells, which limits the translation of research findings into effective clinical therapies. In this study, we developed an ex vivo blood-based model utilizing a versatile nano-delivery platform to evaluate the responsiveness of MDM2 knockout as a representative therapeutic approach in circulating malignant cells (CMCs) from patients stratified by their p53 status. In our genome editing plasmid delivery system (p@RPA), protamine sulfate was combined with a cell-penetrating peptide to condense the CRISPR-Cas9 plasmid into nano-cores. These nano-cores were then coated with chondroitin sulfate shells functionalized with the AS1411 aptamer, enabling the selective recognition of CD44 and/or nucleolin overexpressing malignant cells. Using the same vector, a molecular beacon delivery system (MBs@RPA) co-loaded with MB(MDM2) for probing MDM2 mRNA, MB(TP53) for probing TP53 mRNA and MB(TP73) for probing TP73 mRNA was constructed for the in situ evaluation of biomarker changes induced by genome editing. p@RPA demonstrates satisfactory efficacy in mediating gene editing for MDM2 knockout in malignant cells. Notably, the knockout of MDM2 induces cell cycle arrest and leads to a marked upregulation of anti-tumor TAp73 irrespective of their p53 status. With efficient gene editing and mRNA probing achieved in patient-derived CMCs, we establish an ex vivo platform capable of in situ therapeutic efficacy assessment at single-cell resolution to explicitly reveal the underlying cellular heterogeneity across individual CMCs.
